subject: gk
question: Directive Principles of State Policy comes under which Article?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 36 - 51.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy **(DPSP) come under Articles 36 to 51 of the Indian Constitution. **
 
• These principles serve as **guidelines for the government **to follow while framing laws and policies, aimed at establishing a just society in India.
 
• Although these principles are **non-justiciable** (not enforceable by the courts), they are** fundamental in the governance** of the country.
 
• The DPSPs aim to promote social and economic welfare, including provisions for equal pay for equal work, securing a living wage, free legal aid, and promoting education and public health **(Article 39, 41, 42).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Articles 12 – 35: Fundamental Rights**

__
 
• **Article 12**: Defines the term State for the purpose of enforcement of Fundamental Rights. It includes the government, Parliament, state legislatures, and other authorities.
 
• **Article 13**: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights are void.
 
• **Articles 14-18**: The Right to Equality covers equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination, and abolition of untouchability.
 
• **Articles 19-22**: The Right to Freedom covers speech, assembly, movement, protection in respect of conviction for offenses, and protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• **Articles 23-24**: Protection against exploitation, including human trafficking and forced labor.
 
• **Articles 25-28**: The Right to Freedom of Religion includes freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• **Articles 29-30**: Rights related to Cultural and Educational Freedoms for minorities.
 
• **Articles 31-35**: Include provisions for the Right to Property (later removed as a Fundamental Right), and the Right to Constitutional Remedies under Article 32.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 34: Restriction on Rights during Martial Law**

 
 
• Allows Parliament to impose restrictions on fundamental rights when martial law is in force.
 
• Provides legal protection for acts done under martial law to maintain law and order.
 
 
 
• **Article 35: Legislation for Part III Provisions**
 
 
• Grants Parliament the power to make laws for enforcing certain Fundamental Rights (e.g., abolition of untouchability, prohibition of trafficking).
 
• Ensures Parliament alone can legislate on these matters to maintain uniformity across India.
